facts.fact: Communications Authority Director General David Mugonyi says Kenya promulgated the Cybercrime and Computer Misuse (Critical Information Infrastructure and Cybercrime Management) Regulations in early 2024 to secure critical information infrastructure in sectors such as e-government, telecommunications, banking, transport, energy and health.
facts.system: Cybercrime and Computer Misuse (Critical Information Infrastructure and Cybercrime Management) Regulations

systems.system: Cyber Security Operations Centre for the ICT and Telecommunications Sector
systems.country_label: Cyber Security Operations Centre (ICT and telecoms sector)

KEN.note: Only regulations under the law are mentioned; the document does not state the law's standing or any use.

facts.fact: The Communications Authority says its Sh5 billion programme to lay 2,500 km of fibre across 19 counties for rural internet access is 50 per cent complete with 1,300 km laid, and that over five years it deployed base stations across over 130 sub-locations covering over 750,000 people in 24 counties.
facts.system: Communications Authority rural fibre and BTS programme

systems.system: Communications Authority rural fibre and BTS programme
systems.country_label: CA fibre and mobile connectivity programme

KEN.note: The Authority's Sh5 billion fibre financing is not stated to be a fund assigned by law or a state budget line.
No government online service is described.
No Kenya internet-use share is given; the figures are for the world, low-income countries and Africa.
Mentions a partnership with ICTA and Kenya Power but nothing on government staff running or building systems.
